ANTHONY, 2026-08-14: *"as always is the case is that we are using reflow2 to design itself, but nothing is for reflow2 itself. what we do for reflow2 should be generalizable to whoever is using reflow2 on a project."*

🛑 **THE TEST APPLIED TO WHAT HAD JUST BEEN DONE, AND IT FAILS.** Three DesignRules were created minutes earlier from this session's lessons. **A DesignRule lives in THIS graph and governs THIS design.** A consumer project has its own graph and its own rules; nothing seeds these into it. So all three made the lessons findable BY US and delivered nothing to anybody using reflow2. That is correct for a rule about how this project works — `rule:nothing-lands-on-main-directly` should not travel — but it does NOT discharge a lesson that is general.

⭐ **THE VEHICLES THAT ACTUALLY GENERALISE** are the ones served rather than stored: the SKILLS (compiled into the binary, so every project gets the current one), the TOOL BEHAVIOUR (detectors, report shapes, what a command prints), the served INSTRUCTIONS (`get_instructions`), and the KIT (`reflow2_check.py`, `reflow2_init.py`). reflow2's own graph nodes reach nobody.

═══ ✅ MEASURED: THE `ci-gate` SKILL IS THE GENERAL HOME FOR TODAY'S GATE LESSONS, AND IT IS SILENT ON ALL OF THEM ═══

Read in full 2026-08-14. It is served to every project that wants a design gate, and:

**1. IT INVITES THE ORDERING FAILURE IT DOES NOT WARN ABOUT.** Step 3 says *"Run it locally first (`python3 <kit>/tools/reflow2_check.py --export design.json`) so the first CI run is not the first run."* **Nothing says to run it AFTER committing.** `fact:the-lineage-gate-verdict-depends-on-when-you-run-it` measured the consequence on this project the same day: the identical file FAILED before an amend and PASSED after, because the gate compares against the export committed at HEAD. A user following this skill literally as written gets a verdict about a commit that may be about to change.

**2. IT SAYS NOTHING ABOUT PIPING THE GATE.** `fact:a-piped-gate-reports-the-pipes-exit-code-not-the-gates` is a measured failure on this project — `cargo test | grep | tail` reported success because a pipeline's exit code is its LAST command's. The skill's own CI snippet is unpiped and therefore correct by luck, and a user who pipes it to filter noise gets a green build from `grep`. **`rule:success-is-read-from-the-authoritative-object` was just ENFORCED on Anthony's word, and the skill that configures the gate does not carry it.**

**3. 🛑 IT UNDER-DESCRIBES THE GATE IT CONFIGURES.** *"What it checks, and what makes it fail"* lists exactly two failure modes — unaccepted DRIFT and an open anchored GAP at/above threshold — plus exit 2 for could-not-run. **LINEAGE is not mentioned anywhere**, and a LINEAGE failure is what actually turned this session red (`FAIL LINEAGE 'docs/design/reflow2.json' does not link to the export it replaced`). A user hitting it would find no explanation in the skill that set the gate up, and the skill's *"When the build goes red"* section has no entry for it.

⇒ **SO THE GENERAL FORM OF EVERY GATE LESSON THIS SESSION LEARNED HAS AN EXISTING, SERVED, PROJECT-AGNOSTIC HOME — AND THAT HOME IS CURRENTLY EMPTY ON ALL THREE COUNTS.** The lessons were recorded where they help this project's maintainers and not where they would reach the people the tool is for.

📌 THE GENERAL PRINCIPLE WORTH KEEPING, in his framing: **reflow2 designing itself is a TEST HARNESS, not the point.** Every finding from self-hosting should be asked one question before it is filed — *does this land in the served surface, or only in our own graph?* — and a finding that lands only in our own graph is unfinished work rather than a completed capture. `rule:the-self-host-always-trails-what-it-teaches` is the nearest existing node and says something adjacent but not this: it explains why reflow2's own design lags, not that self-host findings owe a served fix.

⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the other served skills carry the same shape of omission. Only `ci-gate` was read against this session's evidence; `link-artifacts`, `check-health` and `parallel-work` all touch the export and were not checked.
